title: A monic principal open of the affine line is an fppf cover
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $P\in A[T]$ a monic polynomial, meaning that $P=T^d+\sum_{i<d}a_iT^i$ for some integer $d\geq0$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Write $A[T,1/P]=A[T,Y]/(YP-1)$. The canonical morphism $\operatorname{Spec}A[T,1/P]\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and surjective. Thus it is an fppf cover: a flat locally finitely presented surjective morphism. The assertion includes $d=0$ and the zero ring.

source.place: Tag 00FB, lemma-affineline-open, proof: image of D(P) is the union of the principal opens of the coefficients; monic case. Flatness of the polynomial localization and its displayed finite presentation supply the fppf refinement used in Conrad Proposition 4.3.1 and Lemma 4.3.2.

proof.text: Put $B=A[T]$ and $C=B[Y]/(PY-1)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-polynomial-quotient] with $R=B$ and $r=P$: the map fixing $B$ and sending $Y$ to $1/P$ identifies $C$ with $B_P$, compatibly with the maps from $A$. Thus the stated map is the composite $\operatorname{Spec}B_P\to\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$.

The projection $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is flat by [lem-nagata-polynomial-projection-flat], using one variable. The ring map $B\to B_P$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat] for the multiplicative set $\{P^n:n\geq0\}$, which is allowed to contain zero. Its affine spectrum map is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine]. Their composite is flat by [lem-pc-flat-compose].

The algebra $C=A[T,Y]/(YP(T)-1)$ has two generators and one relation over $A$. This is a finite presentation. At every point of $\operatorname{Spec}C$, use the whole source and the whole target as affine neighbourhoods in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Hence the displayed morphism is locally of finite presentation.

By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open], the image of $\operatorname{Spec}B_P\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is exactly $D(P)$. By [lem-sfb-polynomial-basic-open-image-coefficients], a prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$ lies under a point of $D(P)$ iff some coefficient of $P$ is outside $\mathfrak p$. The coefficient of $T^d$ is $1$, and no prime contains $1$. Thus every $\mathfrak p$ is in the image and the composite is surjective. Together with steps 2 and 3 this is an fppf cover by the stated definition. When $d=0$, $P=1$ and $C=A[T]$; for the zero ring both spectra are empty and surjectivity is vacuous.
